exec_summary.text: Claude Haiku 5.5 launched 2026-10-07 (`claude-haiku-5-5`): 1M context, $0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok for prompts of 100K tokens or less, $0.50 / $2.50 above; it is now the default `haiku` alias in Claude Code (v2.1.293). Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were cut from $0.20 to $0.10 the same day.

Anthropic is pushing always-on, multi-agent surfaces: Claude Tag (Slack), Claude Code Projects (beta, Pro/Max), cloud sessions, Managed Agents dynamic workflows (beta, 10-09) and Claude Duet (research preview, waitlist). Cherny describes Tag and Projects as the bets that may eventually replace Claude Code itself.

Claude Code gained Mods (v2.1.287, 2026-10-01), plugins that change rendering, prompts and tool calls, alongside idle compaction, default-on fork subagents, review levels (Quick/Standard/Deep) for the GitHub Code Review service (v2.1.304; org-level, PR-based, distinct from the local `/code-review` command) and a cluster of Windows PowerShell hook fixes.

Platform and ecosystem: API version 2026-10-21 with major-version SDKs (Apache 2.0), Agent Skills donated to the Agentic AI Foundation (10-22), Sonnet 4.5 retirement set for 2026-11-30, and an S-1 filing (10-26).

Grok comparison (first run): the only clean independent head-to-head is LMArena WebDev (2026-10-27, models only), Claude Opus 5.5 1810 vs Grok 4.7 1637. Grok Bot is a different product category from Claude Code and has no independent benchmark.

items.text: Haiku 5.5: first Haiku-class model with an effort parameter; 128k max output; adaptive thinking on by default; on Claude API, Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry. Breaking changes vs Haiku 4.5 return 400s: manual `budget_tokens`, `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`, assistant prefill, `computer_20250124`. (10-07)
Opus 5.5 fast mode left research preview 2026-10-15 (no access request; header optional); also on Microsoft Foundry. The "(research preview)" label was removed from `/fast` in v2.1.304.
Sonnet 4.5 (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`) deprecated; retirement on Claude API 2026-11-30. (09-30)
No Opus, Sonnet or Fable launch posts in the window.

Mods (v2.1.287): a mod is a plugin whose `hook.json` gains a `modules` key pointing at a TypeScript file that registers functions on internal events (render, tool call, permission check, prompt), Express-middleware style; the demo hides email addresses on screen until hover.
Built-in "You should know" mod, a side agent that flags what you or Claude may miss (v2.1.287, first-party sessions with telemetry on).
Idle compaction (v2.1.299): a 200K+ token conversation idle about 54 minutes is compacted before the one-hour prompt cache expires; `"idleCompaction": false` turns it off.
Fork subagents on by default in `claude -p`, Agent SDK, desktop app and VS Code (v2.1.302); Agent tool gets an `effort` parameter (v2.1.292); subagent `autoCompactWindow` (v2.1.296).
Auto mode: `/auto-mode-setup` (v2.1.304), `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` (v2.1.302). Hooks: `onFailure: "block"` (v2.1.295). `ultrathink` now runs its turn at xhigh effort (v2.1.311).
Code Review: Quick / Standard (default) / Deep levels (v2.1.304); `@claude review stop` (v2.1.307).

Windows: PowerShell hooks now block on exit code 2 and fail closed when Git for Windows is missing (v2.1.299, v2.1.309, v2.1.310); git commands faster (v2.1.309, v2.1.304); exFAT/FAT32 write refusals fixed (v2.1.302); PowerShell tool finds plugin `bin/` commands (v2.1.302); stdio MCP servers shut down gracefully (v2.1.296).
Agent Skills open standard donated to the Agentic AI Foundation 2026-10-22; the newsroom index says more than 70 platforms adopted it (index summary only; the post itself was not fetched).
MCP protocol version 2026-07-28 is negotiated by default for stdio servers (v2.1.292) and claude.ai connectors (v2.1.295); `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy` opts out.
Claude Code Projects: one conversation coordinates threads, each a full session on its own branch in the cloud; threads watch PRs and fix CI; daily routine checks; beta, rolling out to Pro and Max.
Cloud sessions: own VM, continue while you are away, start from phone; count toward plan limits with no separate compute charge.
Cloud routines get an effort picker (v2.1.312); cloud sessions and Remote Control can be gated by Enterprise custom roles (v2.1.310).
Claude in a team channel: remembers channel instructions, works from its own accounts, logs every change, asks permission before acting on your behalf; Team and Enterprise.
Changelog adds Slack Connect channels (off by default), Allow once/Deny cards, `!fast`, analytics and spend limits; API beta for Tag settings 2026-10-23.

Chat and Cowork merged into one Claude; Docs, Slides, Design out of beta on all plans including Free (10-19); Dashboards (beta, paid plans) and Motion (beta, Team/Enterprise); Claude Duet (see the Grok section B).

API version 2026-10-21; SDK majors Python 2.0.0, TypeScript 1.0.0, Go 2.0.0, Java 3.0.0, C# 13.0.0, PHP 1.0.0, Ruby 2.0.0, ant CLI 2.0.0; breaking changes independent of API version; licence Apache 2.0 instead of MIT.

Managed Agents: dynamic workflows (beta, `managed-agents-2026-04-01`, 10-09); scheduled deployments on Claude Platform on AWS (10-14); `web_fetch` limited to URLs already in session context (10-07, anti-exfiltration); org-level web fetch off switch (10-20).

User profiles (`/v1/user_profiles`) for per-customer enforcement; OpenTelemetry export beta (10-14); Admin API out of beta (09-30); Claude Models on Google Cloud (10-22); Max and Team plans now include monthly API credits (10-07).

workflows.text: Adversarial review, then a judge. Spin off several Claude threads whose only task is to prove the work wrong, then use another Claude to validate the criticisms; prefer hard outside evidence, because "the current session" is a poor judge of its own work. Rieseberg describes running it in Projects with five threads.

Verification evidence on every PR. Claude does a first-pass review that exercises the change like a user (browser, end-to-end, linting); edit hooks study diffs; team taste lives in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; humans check the agent's evidence (screenshots, video).
Give Claude raw data and tools, not curated slices, and document tools well; "model experience" as a design test. Rieseberg's own caution: upfront setup cost is real.

Be sparing with skills. Rieseberg says Anthropic's official guidance is to be careful because a skill's usefulness decays fast, and removing a skill can improve output; most useful where you have an eval.
Projects economics: coordinator on low effort, threads on a smaller model, switch up for hard tasks; Projects burn plan limits faster than one session.

Sandbox plus auto mode instead of yes/no prompts. Cherny: prompts became "security theater"; a second model without conversation context judges each command. The sandbox is opt-in in Claude Code and on by default in Cowork.

One shared company agent in Slack instead of one agent per person, built on Managed Agents (sandboxes, memory, session control); agent acts as a separate entity but on the requester's behalf for tool calls. Guests are Every staff, not Anthropic.

contradictions.note: No prior baseline report, so nothing retired against a baseline. Within-window contradictions between sources:

items.claim: Auto mode is on by default in every Claude Code session (Krieger).
items.text: The changelog says sessions with no permission mode start in `default` on third-party providers, telemetry-off or fresh installs (v2.1.302), reversing v2.1.285. Primary source wins: treat "on by default everywhere" as wrong, or at best true for some plans.

items.claim: Claude Code prompt-injection success rate is "zero" (Cherny).
items.text: Because none could be demonstrated in a one-week bounty. Staff claim with no primary support in these files; the same sentence concedes vulnerabilities "probably still exist".

grok.contradicted: None found. Unresolved vendor-versus-vendor gaps: Terminal-Bench 4.0 for Fable 5.1 is 57.9 in xAI's table but 55.8 in Anthropic's, and xAI's 57.9 equals the figure Anthropic gives GPT-6 Astra; Artificial Analysis Grok 4.7 Index 34 versus a relay's 46. Anthropic's 66.4% (xhigh) vs the 64.8% mirror (max) is within stated error; xAI's 37.6 vs the 37.58 board entry is consistent. CursorBench is not neutral for xAI because Cursor is reported to be part of its parent.
grok.bottom_line: On the one clean independent head-to-head (LMArena WebDev, 2026-10-27, models only) Claude Opus 5.5 leads Grok 4.7 by 173 points; Terminal-Bench points the same way but rests on mirrors, different harnesses and efforts, so the report does not rank it. Both CLIs ship native Windows installers, but Claude Code has documented data terms and a run of Windows hook fixes in this window, while Grok Build's data terms were not found; Grok Bot is a general always-on work agent with no independent benchmark, and its nearest Claude equivalents (cloud sessions with routines, Tag, Duet) differ in tier and availability, so for solo local Python/R/.qmd work on Windows nothing in tier 1-2 evidence argues for switching from a local Claude Code session (inference).
